context: A developer toolkit has a crash recovery detector that warns when a previous session may have ended abnormally. The detector checks whether any commits exist that are newer than the last saved session state file. The problem: during normal multi-commit development phases, the detector fires on every session start because there are always commits newer than the state file. This produces false positives that train developers to ignore the warning, defeating its purpose.
question: How should the crash recovery detector be fixed to reduce false positives while still catching genuine crashes?
expert_answer: Add a second independent signal: require BOTH that commits are newer than the state file AND that no debrief/wrap-up commit appears in the recent commit history. A normal session ends with a debrief commit, so its absence is a genuine crash indicator.
expert_reasoning: The original single-signal detector (commits newer than state file) has high recall but low precision -- it catches all crashes but also fires on every normal session. The key insight is that normal sessions have a distinguishing artifact: a debrief or wrap-up step that produces a commit. Crashes skip this step. By requiring both conditions (new commits AND no debrief commit), the detector becomes a conjunction of two independent signals, dramatically reducing false positives while preserving true positive detection. This is better than raising the threshold (e.g., requiring N commits newer) because it uses a qualitative signal (presence of wrap-up) rather than a quantitative one (count of commits), which is more robust across different work patterns.
anti_pattern: Raising the commit-count threshold (e.g., 'only warn if 5+ commits are newer'). This trades false positives for false negatives: small sessions that crash won't trigger the warning, and large sessions that complete normally will still trigger it. Threshold tuning is a losing game because it tries to distinguish crash from normal using a single axis (quantity) when the real distinguishing feature is qualitative (did the session end cleanly).
